entities.summary:
Francisco de Remolins was a Spanish Roman Catholic bishop and cardinal from 1480 to 1518. He played a significant role in the Counter-Reformation during the late 16th century, particularly in his native Spain.

 As a prominent figure in the Catholic Church, de Remolins worked closely with Pope Leo X and Pope Julius II to strengthen the Church's position against Protestantism. He also contributed to the publication of several important theological works, including the 'Commentariae in Acta Apostolorum' (Commentaries on the Acts of the Apostles).

 De Remolins' legacy can be seen in the continued influence of the Catholic Church in Spain and its role in shaping European politics during the 16th century. His contributions to the Counter-Reformation helped establish the Church as a dominant force in Western Europe.

 Francisco de Remolins' impact on history was marked by his unwavering dedication to the Catholic faith, which led him to dedicate his life to spreading its teachings and combating the spread of Protestantism during a pivotal moment in world history.
